editorial:
Imagine you are trying to do a huge favor for your girlfriend, but it involves lying to a fancy hotel manager. That is exactly what happens here. You get to follow a smooth-talking PR guy who uses all his charms to convince the posh Ritz hotel to hire his girlfriend's brother as their new chef. The problem is that the brother is not exactly a pro, leading to plenty of chaos and funny misunderstandings. It feels like a lighthearted romp where everything that can go wrong does, but in the most entertaining way possible. The vibe is bubbly, optimistic, and full of that classic old-school charm that makes you feel good.

What really works is the snappy dialogue and the way the actors play off each other. The pacing is quick, so you never feel bored, though some of the jokes might feel a bit dated since it is from 1935. If you love seeing a scheme fall apart in a funny way, you will really enjoy this. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a restored version to get the best picture. You can try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection if you want that crisp look for your movie nights.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the hotel management almost catches the fake chef in his lies. However, through a series of lucky accidents and some great cooking, the brother actually manages to impress the guests. The PR man's plan pays off because the hotel owners decide to keep him on staff. Everyone ends up happy, the couple stays together, and the brother gets a real shot at a career in the kitchen.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic comedies and funny misunderstandings.
